purpose: Eliglustat is used to treat adults with Gaucher disease type 1, a rare inherited condition where a fatty substance builds up in organs like the spleen, liver, and bone marrow. It helps reduce the buildup of this harmful substance in your body. It is taken by mouth, making it a convenient option compared to intravenous treatments.
how_it_works: In Gaucher disease, your body does not break down a certain fatty substance called glucocerebroside properly, so it collects in your organs and causes problems. Eliglustat works by blocking the enzyme that makes this fatty substance in the first place, so less of it is produced and less builds up over time. Think of it like turning down the faucet so the tub does not overflow.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include joint pain, fatigue, nausea, headache, diarrhea, upper respiratory infection, and dizziness. Some people also notice back pain, stomach pain, or a runny nose. Most side effects are mild to moderate.
warnings: Eliglustat can affect your heart rhythm, so it is very important that your doctor checks for certain heart conditions before you start. It cannot be used if you are a poor metabolizer of a liver enzyme called CYP2D6 who also takes certain other medications, so genetic testing is done before starting. Many common medications can interact with eliglustat, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist about everything you take, including over-the-counter drugs and supplements.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one capsule (84 mg) taken by mouth twice a day, with or without food. Your doctor will determine your exact dose based on genetic testing results that show how your body processes this medication. Always swallow the capsule whole and try to take it at the same times each day.
